retracted.why_retracted: derived from the async-off leg's MEAN TPOT, which carries a deterministic ~179 ms stall at ITL index 0 (std_itl 14.1009 against the async-on leg's 0.4025). The median-based gain above is the honest figure; see README 'Why the first A/B had to be redone'

async_scheduling_ab_single_user.note: vLLM 0.24.0 enables async scheduling by default; --no-async-scheduling is the off leg. Async on is faster end-to-end at every output length measured.

named_limitations: No profiler evidence in this stage by rule: no Tracy, tt-perf-report, TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER, live-server device profiling or ReadDeviceProfiler. Device-time and roofline fields are null for that reason, not because they were not attempted.

Per-user decode at max_num_seqs=32 is still ~11.6x slower than at max_num_seqs=1 (230.079 ms against 19.801 ms). The standalone control shows ~229 ms of that is the fixed cost of a decode graph configured 32 rows wide and is independent of how many rows hold requests; removing it needs a variable-width decode graph, which this stage did not attempt.
Async scheduling buys 1.754 ms/token of decode and costs 153.4 ms of TTFT. The shipped configuration keeps vLLM's default (on); a TTFT-sensitive deployment should pass --no-async-scheduling.

A penalised request still pays host-side full-vocabulary operand staging (+14.2%/+25.6% TPOT, stage 08). The 'incremental operand update' stage 08 proposed was re-examined and not taken: the missing slot key turns out to be available, but stage 08's own measurement shows the staging cost is the fixed 9.7 MB operand rather than the history re-derivation, so the incremental update cannot reach it. See README, 'The penalised path'.
